DEVICE: the routing override MHS/registry/overrides/p3-reauthor-routing.json re-selects the pack's OT-2 tool, tools.opentrons2.driver:Ot2Driver (driver.py:10), whose protocol run has a stop (167-181) and a readable status (199-214). The pack's own OT-2 gRPC server leaves the Ot2Driver construction commented out (server.py:24-27). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: a decorated direct Driver, not the PythonObjectDriver helper. R2 (pipetting). SCOPE: run_protocol uploads one operator-approved file, creates a run and plays it (62-123), refused BUSY while this endpoint's previous run is not succeeded, stopped or failed; stop_run (the safe-state action) and the e-stop read the run's status and, unless it is succeeded, stopped or failed (the states that end wait_for_completion, 227-231), send the run action stop and read the status every 0.25 s until it is, for at most 8 s, else the stop fails (SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, latch kept, retried). The run is not deleted (cancel_protocol deletes it right after the stop, 184-190). play is sent under the stop lock after a cancellation check, so an e-stop (which cancels first) never runs between them. With no run of this endpoint the stop reads /health; runs of other clients are not stopped. Reads: the run id and its status (empty before the first run). Not covered: pause, resume, lights, camera, wait_for_completion, the gRPC server, the pack's other tools. LIMITS: protocol is operator_required (an allowed set of exact file paths); the example overlay approves one placeholder path. BOUNDED TRANSPORT: the upstream's requests have no timeout except get_run_status (30 s), and the class inherits ABCToolDriver.__getattr__, which answers any missing name with a no-op (base_server.py:28-34). native.py is therefore a port of Ot2Driver with the upstream's names and requests, each with a connect and a read timeout (deployment options, 3 s and 5 s by default), plus one method of its own, stop: the first request of cancel_protocol without its DELETE. G7 warns MAYBE_ABSENT for stop (not defined on the upstream class; on the upstream class the name would silently do nothing, and the e-stop's status read-back would then fail). The hardware backend never builds the upstream class. FAKE: a dictionary robot server; of its status words only succeeded, stopped, failed and blocked-by-open-door occur in the clone; idle, running and stop-requested, every id and the run duration are placeholders. A transport failure of an effectful request is an unknown outcome. FOR THE HUMAN REVIEWER: the stop's semantics on the robot (how quickly a stopped run reports stopped, what the gantry does) are the Opentrons robot server's and are not shown in this clone; the e-stop waits for at most one play request in flight; consider a permit for run_protocol. A run this endpoint created but never played (an e-stop during the upload cancels the play) is stopped the same way; the clone shows neither the status of such a run nor whether the robot server accepts stop for it (the fake's idle is a placeholder): if the server refuses that stop, the stop fails closed (latch kept, retried) and run_protocol answers Busy until a stop of that run succeeds; verify on a real OT-2. The protocol limit pins exact paths, not file contents: a file replaced after its path was approved runs as it then is, so keep approved files where only the operator can write them.
